question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3' **i.e. **'Highly'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate word to fill in the blank number 3 would be **"highly".**
 
• **The context **of the sentence is emphasizing the high nutritional value of milk.
 
• So, using** "highly"** before **"nutritious"** amplifies this value and appropriately conveys the intended meaning.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *There are so many myths about the negative impacts of milk on health. Changing how much milk you drink because of these myths may mean you are unnecessarily restricting this **highly** nutritious drink. Australians often restrict dairy foods when they try to (4) weight believing them to be fattening. While dairy products naturally contain fat there are many reduced fat products (5) _______.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options are less appropriate:
 
 
• **"Suddenly" **- This adverb describes something happening quickly and unexpectedly. It doesn't fit in this context because the nutritional value of milk is not sudden or unexpected.
 
• **"Nominally" **- This adverb means 'in name only' or 'very little'. It's not suitable in this context because it doesn't effectively emphasize the high nutritional value of milk.
 
• **"Invisibly" **- This adverb means 'in a way that cannot be seen'. It doesn't fit in this context because we're not discussing anything that's unseen or invisible.
